acceptance.assertion: Immediately before prepare-intent and again before apply, GitHub main is freshly observed; the exact target contains this protected authority merge and all then-current legitimate main merges, and required validate (3.10), validate (3.12), registry-registration-preflight/freshness or equivalent protected-main registration checks for that exact revision are successful.

Immediately before prepare-intent and again before apply, a typed precondition readback proves that active deployment-manifest source_commit and canonical Registry source identity are equal, and that this active source is exactly the registered deployed source 38dd8067d1f27c955ba1fca2d42f4eabe1593c0e or a verified Git ancestor of the freshly selected target main commit. Any deployment/Registry identity mismatch, unrelated or diverged source history, unavailable ancestry proof, or target drift blocks the runtime effect fail-closed.

The exact authority TaskSpec is merged through the protected create-only Registry path and adopted missing-only into the authoritative StateStore. The StateStore readback shows this exact task ID nonterminal in ready or active state before any runtime effect; no existing TaskSpec is overwritten or reset.

This authority starts at most one runtime effect. Failed, unclear, timeout or transport-ambiguous outcomes are read back from intent, attempt/result, manifest, launcher, package, snapshot and authority-consumption evidence before any further action; no blind retry is permitted.

After a successful refresh, deployment manifest, immutable release, package tree, launcher pair and canonical Registry snapshot bind the same freshly observed source commit, and Bureau runtime identity and StateStore integrity are valid at that exact target.

After successful convergence, a fresh typed operator-intake proposal or publication preview for one already recorded CATBOT audit candidate is no longer blocked by release-registry-identity-mismatch. This criterion proves only restoration of the normal intake path, not completion of any CATBOT remediation.

The authority is consumed exactly once after successful immutable readback and grants no queue, claim, dispatch, task-supply, product-code, foreign-work or general repository mutation authority. Historical consumed authorities remain terminal and are not reused.
